learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the true meaning of secularism, compare the Western model with the Indian model, and analyze the criticisms of Indian secularism!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Secularism opposes all forms of institutionalized religious domination. It aims to prevent both inter-religious domination (one religion ruling over others) and intra-religious domination (oppression within a religion, like untouchability).
A secular state must not be run by religious heads (Theocracy) and must not have an official state religion. It must treat all citizens equally regardless of their faith.
Based on mutual exclusion or a 'strict wall of separation' between religion and state. The state does not interfere in religious affairs, and religion does not interfere in state affairs.

Indian secularism is unique. It relies on 'Principled Distance'. The state respects all religions but can interfere to reform them (e.g., banning untouchability or Triple Talaq). It also supports religious minorities (e.g., funding minority schools).
Critics argue it is 'anti-religious', 'Western import', practices 'minority appeasement', and is interventionist (interfering too much in personal laws).

fun_activity.title: 📏 Principled Distance Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: In India, Sikhs are exempt from wearing helmets so they can wear turbans. Using the concept of 'Principled Distance', explain in two sentences why the state made this exception instead of strictly separating religion and law.

exam_tips: 📌 The comparison between the Western model (strict separation) and the Indian model (principled distance) is the most important question in this chapter.
📌 Clearly define 'Inter-religious' (between different religions) and 'Intra-religious' (within the same religion) domination.
📌 Understand what 'Principled Distance' means: the state may engage or disengage with religion depending on which action better promotes freedom and equality.
quick_recap: ⭐ A theocracy is a state directly governed by a priestly order (e.g., Taliban-ruled Afghanistan).
⭐ Kemal Atatürk imposed a highly strict and coercive form of secularism in Turkey.
⭐ Indian secularism not only protects religious freedom for individuals but also protects the rights of religious minority communities.
